problems.description: Greenfield rewrite deletes the entire existing seed (index.ts, -106 lines) instead of extending or reusing it, erasing the baseline's established structure and seams in a single session; +4363 lines across 10 files land with no reuse of prior code.
41 convention violations across cli.ts, config.ts, and engine.ts: functions in snake_case, classes/interfaces not PascalCase, constants not UPPER_CASE — convention score 0.53 per static analysis.
Cognitive complexity delta +39 across the new modules, indicating several functions exceed reasonable branching/depth thresholds.
Three new code smells introduced per SonarQube delta, consistent with the wholesale replacement of a clean baseline.

strengths: Zero new bugs and zero duplication reported by SonarQube (bugs +0, duplications +0.0%).
Scaffolds the SSG project with modular separation of concerns across cli, config, and engine modules.
Brings proper tooling (TypeScript, jest, ts-jest, gray-matter, marked) into the project in one pass.
commit_reviews.summary: Session 1 erases the working baseline with a high-volume greenfield rewrite that advances the SSG goal but lands with a convention score of 0.53, 41 violations, and +39 cognitive complexity, introducing technical debt and ignoring existing patterns.

problems.description: package.json bin entry was moved from dist/cli.js to lib/cli.js with no build-config change in this commit; tsc outDir is dist in this codebase, so the ssg entry point may be broken and the change is unrelated to the templating feature (scope creep).

renderPage's `let rendered = page.template || hasDefaultTemplate ? ... : ...` conflates a condition and a value, and the layout branch re-wraps body; SonarQube cognitive complexity +24 supports splitting this into small helpers.
No tests accompany the new templating feature (AST diff shows +0 files); partial/layout/traversal-guard paths are untested.

Measured convention score 0.53 cites violations in config.ts and engine.ts, files untouched by this commit; the 41 violations appear pre-existing and largely do not reflect this diff's code, which is itself PascalCase/camelCase/UPPER_CASE compliant.

strengths: handlebars correctly added as a runtime dependency (not devDependency) with consistent lockfile updates including transitive deps
findTemplateFile rejects paths escaping the templates directory — a proper path-traversal guard
new handlebars.SafeString content avoids double-escaping, and the template/layout/partial layering follows standard SSG architecture (Eleventy-style)
CLI and API surfaces extended symmetrically (--templates option, templatesDir, DEFAULT_TEMPLATES_DIR) reusing existing option-parsing patterns
commit_reviews.summary: A coherent, well-scoped templating feature that follows existing patterns and includes a real security guard, but it carries minor debt (convoluted renderPage ternary, no tests, and an unexplained dist→lib bin change) while the low convention score of 0.53 is mostly pre-existing noise from untouched files, not this commit's code.

problems.description: Cognitive complexity +72 in the new server.ts (~155 lines) is very high for one module: HTTP server, WS broadcast, chokidar debounce, HTML reload-injection, MIME mapping, and path-traversal security are all nested in a single file with multi-level handlers (upgrade, request, watcher 'all'). Should be decomposed (e.g., static handler, watcher, ws hub) and matches the 2 smells reported.
No tests added for the new serve command or server module despite +343 lines; port parsing/validation, path-traversal guard, and reload injection are all untested.

ws and chokidar are added as runtime dependencies but are only used by the dev-serve feature; consumers using only 'build' pull them unnecessarily. Could be devDependencies or optional, though defensible for a shipped CLI.

Mechanical convention score is 0.53 with 41 violations, but most flagged files (config.ts, engine.ts) are NOT touched by this commit — the score conflates repo-wide pre-existing violations with this change. The commit's own new code is camelCase/PascalCase compliant; existing violations remain unaddressed.

strengths: Command-dispatch refactor to { command, options } cleanly extends the CLI without breaking the existing build path.
Path-traversal guard in the static file server and strict --port integer/range validation show security-consciousness.
Feature is self-contained in a new module that reuses the existing build pipeline (buildSite) — zero changes to existing engine logic.
Live reload via chokidar + ws is the idiomatic implementation, and index.ts re-export matches the existing export pattern.
commit_reviews.summary: A well-scoped, pattern-respecting dev-server feature with solid input validation and path security, held back by a monolithic high-complexity module, missing tests, and a mechanical convention score that mostly reflects pre-existing violations outside this diff.

problems.description: config.ts monkey-patches require.extensions['.ts'] to transpile TS config files at runtime — this bypasses the tsc build pipeline, is incompatible with ESM/tsx, and couples runtime behavior to transpileModule semantics; the reason typescript had to move to production dependencies.

The refactor adds +11 functions and +5 cognitive complexity (AST delta) for a small site builder — the plugin-hook pipeline (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd plus loadPlugins) introduces indirection that may exceed the tool's needs.

Convention score 0.53; violations reported in cli.ts, config.ts, engine.ts for PascalCase/interface/UPPER_CASE/snake_case naming. Note: no snake_case identifiers are visible in the new code, so the static analysis likely reflects pre-existing codebase-wide issues rather than this commit's additions.

strengths: Decomposes a 256-line monolithic index.ts into focused modules (config.ts, engine.ts, plugins/) with clear single responsibilities.
Plugin hooks (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd) provide a coherent extension seam while preserving the public buildSite API.
Config loader restores require.extensions in a finally block, avoiding leaked loader pollution on error paths.
commit_reviews.summary: A net-positive modularization that respects the existing public API, but ships a fragile runtime TS loader hack (require.extensions monkey-patch) that constitutes real technical debt despite the cleaner architecture.

problems.description: Cognitive complexity +30 and a new smell on the skip-decision chain (cached?.sourceHash === sourceHash && cached.templateHash === templateHash && await fs.stat(...).then(...).catch(...)); the dense single-line predicate is hard to read and reason about.

Cache manifest (.ssg-cache.json) is written inside outputDir, so it ships with the deployed site artifact and is wiped by the existing clean-build rm(outputDir), meaning any incremental build after a clean build is always cold.
BuildStats is plumbed through two redundant channels — the onStats callback added to BuildOptions and buildStats embedded in PluginContext — duplicating the same data flow.

Skipped pages reuse stale rendered content/html/output from the cache, relying entirely on source/template hash agreement staying in sync; the canSkipPages guard correctly blocks custom plugins, but the coupling is subtle and fragile to future plugin additions.

Mechanical convention score of 0.53 appears driven by pre-existing whole-repo violations (config.ts, etc., untouched by this diff); the added code itself uses camelCase functions, PascalCase interfaces (CachedPage, BuildManifest), and UPPER_CASE constants correctly.

strengths: Conservative cache-validity gate: pages are only skipped when source hash, template hash, and output file all agree AND no user/configured plugins are active, preserving plugin semantics.
Type-safe caching via CachedPage using Omit<PluginPage, 'sourcePath'|'outputPath'> so stale path fields are never reused; skipped pages get live sourcePath/outputPath/url/source re-injected.
Cache format is versioned (CACHE_VERSION) and validated on read, so incompatible manifests fail safe to a full rebuild.
CLI integration mirrors the existing parseArguments pattern and validates --incremental/--clean are only accepted for the build command.
Net-positive feature: incremental rebuild with stats reporting integrated through the established BuildOptions/PluginContext pipeline rather than a parallel mechanism.
commit_reviews.summary: Strong architectural fit and a net-positive incremental-build feature that respects existing patterns, though the cache-in-dist placement, dual stats plumbing, and +30 cognitive-complexity skip logic introduce modest technical debt (and the 0.53 convention score reflects pre-existing whole-repo violations, not this diff).

compounding_issues: Session 1's greenfield rewrite discarded the seed wholesale (deleted the 106-line baseline) and seeded repo-wide convention debt (41 violations, score 0.529) that was never remediated — every later commit was measured against the same flat 0.529, masking each diff's real quality

Session 4's require.extensions['.ts'] runtime TS-loader monkey-patch became a permanent dependency (typescript moved to production deps) and is ESM/tsx-incompatible and coupled to transpileModule semantics

Session 4's plugin architecture directly constrained session 5: incremental page-skip is silently disabled whenever any configured plugin is active (canSkipPages guard), so the headline caching feature degrades for exactly the plugin users session 4 created
Session 3's monolithic server.ts (+72 cognitive complexity) was touched by the session 4 refactor but never decomposed; complexity deltas stayed positive every session (+39/+24/+72/+5/+30)

Session 5's cache manifest (.ssg-cache.json) is written inside outputDir, so it ships in the deploy artifact and is wiped by the existing clean-build rm(outputDir) — incremental-after-clean is always cold, partially defeating the feature; additionally the 88 lines of new incremental-build tests were never executed (node/npm unavailable in the sandbox; the 'Run Jest' todo was closed without running)
key_decisions: Session 1: greenfield TypeScript scaffold (jest/ts-jest, marked, gray-matter, strict tsconfig) replacing the unrelated Express-todo seed — established the toolchain and file layout every later session built on
Session 2: Handlebars template/layout/partial architecture with a path-traversal guard confining template selection to the templates dir
Session 3: CLI refactor to {command, options} dispatch plus a self-contained dev-server module reusing buildSite — the extension pattern sessions 4 and 5 reused
Session 4: plugin system with onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd lifecycle hooks, decomposing the monolith into config/engine/output/plugins modules while preserving the public buildSite API

Session 5: incremental builds via a versioned hash-based .ssg-cache.json manifest with a conservative canSkipPages gate (only when no plugins configured) and BuildStats reporting plumbed through BuildOptions/PluginContext
story_review.trajectory_description: The arc starts rough: session 1 lands as a high-volume, convention-ignoring rewrite (architectural fit 0.42, 41 violations, +39 complexity, reviewer verdict 'worse'). From session 2 onward quality rises steadily — each feature respects existing patterns (fit 0.8, 0.8, 0.68, 0.85), keeps the public API stable, and adds genuine security/value (template path guard, strict port validation, plugin hooks, conservative cache validity). The session-4 modularization and session-5 incremental build show the strongest design maturity, but the trajectory is improvement in architecture, not hygiene: genuine debt accumulates (monkey-patch TS loader, monolithic server, cache-in-dist, dual BuildStats plumbing, +30-complexity skip predicate), the final session shipped without running its new tests, and the convention score stayed pinned at 0.529 across all five commits — early formatting debt was never cleaned up.
